Race analysis across Zwift, ZwiftPower and ZwiftRacing.app

race-analysis.Rmd

This walkthrough answers one question end to end: for a given race, does a rider’s ZwiftRacing.app rating predict where they finished? It touches all three sources — finishers from ZwiftPower, ratings from ZwiftRacing.app, and a spot-check against the Zwift game API — and leans on the cache so repeated runs don’t re-hit the servers.

Credentials

Put these in ~/.Renviron (never in code you commit), then restart R:

ZWIFT_USERNAME=you@example.com
ZWIFT_PASSWORD=...
ZR_AUTH=your-zwiftracing-key     # sent as the x-api-key header
ZP_SID=...                       # phpbb3_lswlk_sid cookie from zwiftpower.com
library(zwiftverse)
library(dplyr)

The field names returned by each API are not stable or documented, so the first thing to do with any new endpoint is look at what came back:

zp  <- zp_set_cookie(zp_session(), Sys.getenv("ZP_SID"))
race_id <- 5795672L        # a completed race (ZwiftPower id = Zwift event id)

res <- zp_result(zp, race_id)
dplyr::glimpse(res)        # confirm the id / position / category column names

The ZwiftPower columns used below (zwid, name, position_in_cat, category, avg_wkg) are confirmed against live data.

1. Finishers from ZwiftPower

zp_result() returns one row per finisher. ZwiftPower ships most numbers as [value, flag] pairs (they arrive as list-columns), so run zp_unflag() first, then pull the rider id, finishing position and category. Column names below were verified against live responses (2026-11).

finishers <- res |>
  zp_unflag() |>
  transmute(
    zwid     = as.integer(zwid),          # ZwiftPower rider id
    name,
    position = as.integer(position_in_cat),
    category,
    wkg_avg  = as.numeric(avg_wkg)
  ) |>
  arrange(category, position)

finishers

2. Ratings from ZwiftRacing.app (one call)

ZwiftRacing.app scores the same race, so its event endpoint already carries every finisher’s rating going into the race — no per-rider lookups needed. zr_result() flattens all pens into one row per rider. ZwiftRacing keys events on the Zwift event id, which is usually the same number as the ZwiftPower id.

zr <- zr_client()

ratings <- zr_result(zr, race_id) |>
  transmute(
    zwid       = as.integer(riderId),
    zr_current = ratingBefore,          # ZR rating before the race
    zr_after   = rating,                # ...and after it
    zr_velo    = riderVelo.race         # vELO rating
  )

ratings

These column names were verified against the live v2 API (2026-11). For riders outside a single race, zr_rider() returns the current profile (vELO rating under velo$race), and zr_rider_overview() the legacy live / max30 / max90 ratings:

library(tidyr)
zr_riders(zr, finishers$zwid[1:5]) |>      # one request per rider (no v2 batch)
  hoist(velo, zr_velo = "race") |>
  select(riderId, zr_velo)

3. Join and analyse 

race <- finishers |>
  left_join(ratings, by = "zwid")

race |> count(is.na(zr_current))   # how many finishers had no ZR rating?

Within a category, does a higher pre-race rating go with a better finish? A rank correlation is the honest summary here — rating and position are both ordinal and the relationship is monotonic, not linear.

race |>
  filter(!is.na(zr_current)) |>
  group_by(category) |>
  summarise(
    n       = dplyr::n(),
    rho     = cor(zr_current, position, method = "spearman"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

A strong negative rho means the favourites (higher rating) finished nearer the front — i.e. the result went to form.

library(ggplot2)

race |>
  filter(!is.na(zr_current)) |>
  ggplot(aes(zr_current, position, colour = category)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_y_reverse() +                     # position 1 at the top
  labs(x = "ZwiftRacing rating (pre-race)", y = "Finishing position",
       colour = "Category",
       title = sprintf("Race %d: rating vs finish", race_id)) +
  theme_minimal()

4. Cross-check against the Zwift game API

ZwiftPower and ZwiftRacing.app both derive from Zwift, so the game API is the tie-breaker when a number looks off. Here we confirm the winner’s category enforcement FTP straight from source:

za     <- zwift_auth()
winner <- race |> filter(category == "A", position == 1) |> pull(zwid)

zwift_profile(za, winner) |>
  select(any_of(c("firstName", "lastName", "ftp", "competitionMetrics")))

Caching notes

Everything above is cached on disk, keyed on method + URL + body:

zv_cache_info()                       # what's stored, how big, how old

# Completed races never change — cache the heavy pulls permanently:
res     <- zp_result(zp, race_id, ttl = Inf)
zr_race <- zr_result(zr, race_id, ttl = Inf)

# Force-refresh a single call:
zr_rider(zr, winner, ttl = 0)

# ...or wipe everything with zv_cache_clear()

A rider’s rating history (no snapshot endpoint in v2) comes from zr_rider_velo():

zr_rider_velo(zr, winner, days = 365, parse = "json")$data$history |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |>
  head()

Caveats

These are reverse-engineered APIs. Field names can shift under you, personal data is GDPR-consent-gated (non-consenting riders simply won’t appear), and the ZwiftPower cookie login is the brittle link — if zp_login() fails, fall back to zp_set_cookie() with a value copied from your browser.
